info.name: AI Customer Support API
info.description:
HTTP APIs for the TypeScript backend (`apps/api`).

**Setup**
1. Import this collection and `local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select the **AI Customer Support — Local** environment.
3. Keep cookies enabled (Postman → Cookies). Login, email verify, and Google complete set `access_token` and `refresh_token` httpOnly cookies.

**Auth flow**
1. Register
2. Copy the verification token from the API logs (development console email) into `verificationToken`
3. Verify email (sets session cookies)
4. Call Get current user, Refresh, or Logout

Passwords must be at least 12 characters and include a letter and a number.

Google OAuth: Start Google sign-in → open `googleAuthorizationUrl` in a browser → after redirect, put the `code` query value into `googleLoginCode` → Complete Google sign-in.

**Organizations / RBAC**
Tenant routes require a session cookie and membership in that organization. Send `x-tenant-id` as the organization id (must match the path when both are present).
1. Create organization (saves `organizationId`)
2. Invite a teammate — copy `?token=` from the API logs into `invitationToken`
3. Preview invitation (public) then Accept invitation while signed in as `inviteEmail`
4. List members, change roles, audit logs

Roles: `owner`, `admin`, `agent`, `viewer`. Invite roles cannot be `owner`.

**Conversations**
Tenant routes under `/api/organizations/:organizationId/conversations`. Requires session cookies and `x-tenant-id`.
1. Create organization, then Create conversation (saves `conversationId`)
2. Send message, add tag, add internal note
3. Assign / unassign, change status, escalate
4. List/search with `q`, `status`, `assignedAgentId`, `tag`, pagination

Permissions: `conversation.read` (viewer+), `conversation.write` (agent+), `conversation.assign`, `conversation.escalate`.
Status: `open` → `pending` | `resolved` | `closed` | `escalated`. Closed conversations reject new messages until reopened.

request.description: Process liveness. Returns 200 even if PostgreSQL or Redis are down.
Infrastructure readiness for PostgreSQL and Redis. 200 when both are up, 503 otherwise.
Creates an unverified account and sends a verification email. In development the verify URL is logged by the console email adapter. Does not set session cookies.
Sends a new verification link if an unverified password account exists. Always returns a generic success message.
Consumes the email verification token from the link (`?token=`). Sets `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies and returns the verified user.
Password login. Email must already be verified. Sets `access_token` and `refresh_token` cookies. Rate limited per IP and email.
Returns the authenticated user. Requires a valid `access_token` cookie or `Authorization: Bearer` access token.
Rotates the refresh token using the `refresh_token` cookie and issues a new access cookie. Reusing a previous refresh token revokes the whole family.
Revokes the current refresh session and clears auth cookies. Returns 204.
Requests a password reset email. Always returns a generic success message. In development the reset URL is logged by the console email adapter — copy `?token=` into `resetToken`.
Sets a new password, revokes all refresh sessions, and clears cookies. Then sign in with `newPassword`.
Returns a Google authorization URL with PKCE. Open `authorizationUrl` in a browser. Requires `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`.

Google redirects here after consent. The API exchanges the OAuth code, then redirects to the web app with a one-time login code. Normally invoked by Google, not Postman. Disable auto-follow redirects to inspect the Location header.
Exchanges the one-time login code from `/auth/callback?code=` for session cookies. The code is single-use and expires quickly.

item.name: Organizations
item.description: Multi-tenant workspaces. Create/list do not need `x-tenant-id`. All `/:organizationId` routes authenticate, resolve tenant membership, and check RBAC. The path id must match `x-tenant-id` when the header is sent.

request.description: Creates an organization and makes the current user the owner. Requires a session cookie. 201 `{ organization }` including `membership.role` and `membership.permissions`.
Lists organizations the authenticated user belongs to, with their role and permissions. Does not include other tenants.
Returns the organization and the caller's membership. Requires `organization.read`. Cross-tenant ids return 403 `UNAUTHORIZED_ORGANIZATION_ACCESS`.
Updates name and/or slug. Requires `organization.update` (owner or admin). Slug must be 3–48 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens.
Removes the current user from the organization. The last owner cannot leave (409 `LAST_OWNER`). Returns 204.
Tenant-scoped member list. Requires `organization.read`. Never returns another organization's members.

exec: const other = members.find((member) => member.userId !== members.find((item) => item.role === 'owner')?.userId) || members[0];

request.description: Changes another member's role. Requires `organization.members.manage`. You cannot change your own role. Only an owner can grant or revoke `owner`. Role: `owner` | `admin` | `agent` | `viewer`.
Removes another member. Requires `organization.members.manage`. Cannot remove yourself (use Leave) or the last owner. Returns 204.

Sends a team invitation. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`. Role must be `admin`, `agent`, or `viewer` (not `owner`). In development the accept URL is logged — copy `?token=` into `invitationToken`.
Lists pending invitations for this tenant. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`.
Public preview of an invitation (organization name, invited email, role, expiry). No auth. Invalid or expired tokens return 400 `INVALID_INVITATION_TOKEN`.
Accepts the invitation for the signed-in user. The session email must match the invited address. Does not use `x-tenant-id` — tenant comes from the invitation.
Revokes a pending invitation. Requires `organization.invitations.manage`. Returns 204.

Tenant-scoped audit log. Requires `organization.audit.view` (owner or admin). Query: `page` (min 1), `pageSize` (1–100). Actions include `organization.created`, `organization.member.invited`, `organization.invitation.accepted`, `organization.member.role_changed`.

Creates an open conversation for a customer. Requires `conversation.write`. Optional: subject, channel (`web` | `email` | `api`), tags, assignedAgentId, initialMessage, initialMessageAuthor (`customer` | `agent`).
Paginated inbox search. Requires `conversation.read`. Query: `page`, `pageSize` (1–100), `q` (subject, customer, tags, message body), `status`, `assignedAgentId` (user id or `unassigned`), `tag`.
Loads one tenant-scoped conversation with tags and assignee. Requires `conversation.read`.
Assigns an active owner, admin, or agent in this organization. Requires `conversation.assign`.
Clears the assignee. Requires `conversation.assign`.

Transitions status. Requires `conversation.write`. Allowed: `open`, `pending`, `resolved`, `closed`. Use Escalate for `escalated`. Closed conversations cannot accept messages until reopened to `open`.
Escalates an `open` or `pending` conversation. Requires `conversation.escalate`. Optional reason (max 500).
Adds a tag (1–32 lowercase letters, numbers, or hyphens; max 20 tags). Requires `conversation.write`.
Removes a tag from the conversation. Requires `conversation.write`.
Adds a message. Requires `conversation.write`. `authorType` defaults to `agent` (use `customer` to log a customer reply). Closed conversations return 409 `CONVERSATION_CLOSED`.
Paginated messages in chronological order. Requires `conversation.read`.
Adds an internal note (not a customer-visible message). Requires `conversation.write`.
Paginated internal notes. Requires `conversation.read`.
